lines.japanese: 目を覚ました新しい俺たち、二日目の朝。
lines.english: Morning two since the new us awoke.

lines.japanese: 昨日は実験的な一日だった。言ってみれば今日からが真・俺たち。
lines.english: Yesterday had been an experiment. You might say the real us began today.

lines.japanese: さあ今日も薔薇色の一日を始めるぞ、元気出していこう俺たち。ていうか俺。
lines.english: Time to begin another rose-colored day. Come on, us, let's show some spirit. I mean, me.

lines.japanese: 「コンドルワ！」
lines.english: “Condorvening!”

lines.japanese: あれ、口が勝手に開いた。うーん、奈落者がふたりも入ってるせいで、昨日からときおり奇抜な言動が漏れるな……。
lines.english: Huh. My mouth had opened on its own. Hmm. With two denizens of the Abyss inside me, the odd outlandish word or deed had been leaking out since yesterday...

lines.japanese: まあいい、そのうち落ちつくだろう。ともあれ俺たち二日目の朝は始まった。とは言っても──
lines.english: Oh, well. It would settle down eventually. In any case, the second morning of our life had begun. Although—

lines.japanese: ──昨日ほどの感動はないな。ま、それが正常な反応か。日々いちいち朝を迎えるたびに感動してたら、逆にそっちの方が異常だ。なあ、そうだろみんな……いやだから俺は俺ひとりだって。
lines.english: —it was not as moving as yesterday. Which was probably the normal response. If every ordinary morning moved me to tears, that would be the abnormal thing. Right, everyone...? No, I keep telling you: there is only one of me.

lines.japanese: どうもまだ俺という意思が一つにまとまってないな。まあ、まだ二日目だ。もともと強引に進めた統合が、そう最初から上手くまとまるはずもない。
lines.english: My will had not yet cohered into a single *me*. Still, this was only day two. An integration forced through in the first place could hardly be expected to hold together perfectly from the start.

lines.japanese: そうだ、これから先は長い。たぶん長い。焦らず地道にやっていこう。
lines.english: Yes. We had a long road ahead. Probably. No need to rush; we would work at it steadily.

lines.japanese: いまの俺は、ひとりの平凡な青少年として、ごく普通の生活を送ることだけ意識しよう。
lines.english: For now, I would think only of living a perfectly ordinary life as one ordinary young man.

lines.japanese: よし、じゃあ次にやるべきはなんだ？　難しく考えることはない。平凡な青少年が朝、目を開けて次にすることはなんだ？　そう、布団から出て立ちあがればいいだけだ。
lines.english: Good. What came next? There was no need to complicate matters. What did an ordinary young man do after opening his eyes in the morning? Why, he simply threw off the bedding and stood up.

lines.japanese: 「チェスト！」
lines.english: “Hyaaah!”

lines.japanese: 気合一閃。俺は布団を蹴りあげ、天井めがけて跳びあがった。
lines.english: With a single explosive cry, I kicked off the covers and sprang toward the ceiling.

lines.japanese: いささか平凡な起床方法ではない気もするが、なにせお兄ちゃんパワーに起因する過剰な万能感と高揚感が、俺のテンションを無駄に釣りあげているのだ。かくも清々しい朝、じっとしてなどおれぬわ。ぶもははは。
lines.english: Admittedly, this did not seem an altogether ordinary way to get up. But the excessive omnipotence and exhilaration produced by Big Brother Power had driven my spirits to useless heights. On so bracing a morning, I could hardly sit still. Bmohahaha!

lines.japanese: さあ、いざ行かん。階下からは香ばしい匂いが漂ってくる。きっと麗しのプリンセス・ダヴが朝食のトーストを焼いているに違いない。
lines.english: Onward, then. A savory smell drifted up from downstairs. No doubt the radiant Princess Dove was toasting our breakfast.

lines.japanese: しかしふすまを開けようとしたところで、ふと布団を畳まなくちゃという思いが訪れた。では畳もうと振りかえれば、今度はとたんに億劫だという思いが訪れる。
lines.english: But just as I reached for the sliding door, it occurred to me that I ought to fold my bedding. The moment I turned back to do it, the thought arrived that it was far too much trouble.

lines.japanese: だって面倒くさくねえ？　はー、そーだいねー。いや駄目だよ、生活の乱れはこうした些細なことから始まるんだ。それにネットで見たんだけど、万年床はカビの繁殖を招くっていう説もあってね。
lines.english: I mean, what a pain in the ass. Yeah, totally. No, this won't do. A disorderly life begins with little lapses like this. Besides, I read online that leaving your bedding down all day encourages mold.

lines.japanese: 俺は朝っぱらからさっそく葛藤していた。やはり統合はまだ完璧じゃないようだ。
lines.english: It was first thing in the morning, and already I was wrestling with myself. The integration clearly remained imperfect.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、小鳩！」
lines.english: “Good morning, Kobato!”

lines.japanese: 俺はお歌のおにいさん的なトーンでごあいさつした。
lines.english: I delivered the greeting in the relentlessly cheerful voice of a children's TV presenter.

lines.japanese: 「あ……お、おはようっ！」
lines.english: “Oh... G-good morning!”

lines.japanese: プリンセス・ダヴあらため俺の可愛い妹は、やはり朝食の準備をしてくれていたみたいだ。台所と居間の間をせかせか行ったり来たりしている。
lines.english: Princess Dove—or rather, my adorable little sister—had indeed been making breakfast. She bustled back and forth between the kitchen and living room.

lines.japanese: 俺は小鳩の邪魔にならないよう、座卓の隅に腰を下ろした。テレビが点いていたので、好奇心いっぱいな男の子であるところの俺はそのニュース番組に注意を寄せてみる。
lines.english: I sat at one corner of the low table, careful not to get in her way. The television was on, so, being a boy brimming with curiosity, I turned my attention to the news.

lines.japanese: 嘘くさい胸の女性アナにコメントを求められ、眼鏡の中年男性がしたり顔で答える。彼らは群れることで気持ちが大きくなるんでしょうな。ふむふむ、なんの話だ？
lines.english: A female anchor with a suspiciously artificial chest asked for comment, and a bespectacled middle-aged man answered with a knowing look. ‘They grow bolder in packs, you see.’ Hmm, hmm. What was this about?

lines.japanese: 「げっ！」
lines.english: “Gah!”

lines.japanese: 画面がモザイク入りのヤンキー集団に切りかわった。右上に参考映像という四文字。どっかで見たようなシルエットの不良集団が、加工されたアヒル声でヨウだのヤーマンだの超パネェだのと騒いでいる。
lines.english: The picture cut to a gang of delinquents with their faces mosaicked out. REFERENCE FOOTAGE appeared in the upper right. A suspiciously familiar set of silhouettes clamored in electronically distorted duck voices: Yo! What up! This is off the hook! And more of the same.

lines.japanese: 「あわわわわ……」
lines.english: “Oh no no no...”

lines.japanese: そのうちに「成田っち見てる～」などという声も聞こえた気がするけれど、そう思った瞬間にはもうチャンネルを変えていたので俺の錯覚だったかもしれない。
lines.english: Before long, I thought I heard somebody shout, ‘Narita, you watching?’ But I had changed the channel the instant the thought occurred, so perhaps I had imagined it.

lines.japanese: 駄目だ駄目だ、けしからん。こんな有害映像、うちの小鳩の情操教育によろしくない。俺は端から入念に選局して、ほがらかに着ぐるみが踊る良い子向け番組に落ちつけた。
lines.english: No, no. Outrageous. Such harmful footage was unfit for Kobato's moral education. I worked meticulously through the channels and settled on a wholesome children's program where cheerful mascots danced.

lines.japanese: 「おまたせっ」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting!”

lines.japanese: 食卓の前で正座していたら、ふっ、と正面に黒い影がよぎった。
lines.english: As I knelt properly before the table, a dark shadow crossed my field of view.

lines.japanese: ことっ。
lines.english: Clink.

lines.japanese: 俺の前にマグカップと白いプレートが置かれる。
lines.english: A mug and a white plate appeared before me.

lines.japanese: トースト、目玉焼き、火を通したベーコンにウインナーソーセージ。パン一枚きりの小鳩の皿より賑やかなメニューが俺の献立だった。
lines.english: Toast, a fried egg, cooked bacon, and small sausages. My plate was far livelier than Kobato's, which held a single slice of bread.

lines.japanese: 「ややっ、ふむん？」
lines.english: “Why, what's this?”

lines.japanese: 俺は大げさに首を振って、メニューの異なる自分と妹の食膳とを交互に見比べてみせる。小鳩がそのリアクションの意図に気付いて、首と右手をぶんぶん横に振った。
lines.english: With exaggerated sweeps of my head, I compared my breakfast with my sister's much plainer setting. Kobato grasped the point of the performance and waved both her head and her right hand furiously.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ううん、いいの。私、あの、あんまりおなか空いてないから」
lines.english: “Oh, no, it's okay. I'm, um... not very hungry.”

lines.japanese: 「なにっ！」
lines.english: “What!”

lines.japanese: 俺の中の五つの魂が色めきたった。当然だ。彼女は我らすべてにとって護るべき姫なのだから。
lines.english: The five souls within me bristled as one. Naturally. To all of us, she was a princess to be protected.

lines.japanese: 「だっ、大丈夫か小鳩！　食欲がないだって？　具合が悪いのか、医者に診てもらうか、病院までおぶって行こうか。でもこういうときはね、食べたくなくても頑張って食べた方がいいんだ、ほら栄養つけないと」
lines.english: “A-are you all right, Kobato? No appetite? Are you sick? Do you need a doctor? Shall I carry you to the hospital? At times like this, though, you have to make yourself eat even if you don't want to. You need your nourishment.”

lines.japanese: 俺は自分のウインナーソーセージを、小鳩のトーストの上にひょいと載せた。
lines.english: I picked up one of my sausages and deposited it upon Kobato's toast.

lines.japanese: 「えっ。い、いいよ、お兄ちゃん食べなよ」
lines.english: “What? N-no, you eat it, big bro.”

lines.japanese: 「うっ、ううう、なんて奥ゆかしくて良い子なのかしら小鳩さんは。お兄ちゃん感激だわ……ううん、でも遠慮しなくていいんだよ。ほら食べなさい食べなさい。食べろッつってんだろ、てめブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Oh my, what a sweet, modest little darling Miss Kobato is. Big Brother is overcome... No, no, you mustn't hold back. Go on, eat. Eat up. I said eat the fucking thing or I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「も、もぉー遠慮してるのはお兄ちゃんでしょー。なに、好き嫌い多いくせにえらそうぶってー」
lines.english: “Y-you're the one holding back! You're so picky, but you still act all superior.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の箸がぱっぱと動いてソーセージを俺の皿へ戻す。
lines.english: Kobato's chopsticks darted out and returned the sausage to my plate.

lines.japanese: 「ああーもうー！　なにー！　なんで兄ちゃんのゆうこと素直にきけないのー。あげるって言ってんだからワァーイってゆって食べなちゃメーでしょもー」
lines.english: “Oh, come ooon! What's this? Why can't you be a good girl and do what Big Brother says? If someone gives you something, you say yaaay and eat it, or you're a naughty girl. Honestly!”

lines.japanese: 「だっ、駄目だよ。お兄ちゃんが好き嫌いしないならいいけど……そんなんじゃ、キュウリとか自分の嫌いなものばっかり私に押しつけるつもりでしょ」
lines.english: “N-no. If you weren't such a picky eater, maybe. You're just going to dump all the things you hate on me, like cucumbers.”

lines.japanese: 「なっ！　なぁー！　なぁーに言ってんの、そ、そんなキュウリとかそんな、兄ちゃんがそんな、す、好き嫌いなんてそんな、す、するはずないでしょー。ナマイキゆうんじゃありません、もぉポッポはー」
lines.english: “Wh-what! Whaaat are you talking about? Cucumbers? Your big brother would never, never be such a... picky eater. Don't talk back, Poppo. Honestly!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ポッポ……」
lines.english: “What? Poppo...?”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: しまった……ヨージ面が強く出過ぎて、うっかり子供のころの仇名で呼んでしまった。背伸びしたい盛りの小鳩にはちょっと屈辱だったかしら。
lines.english: Damn... Too much of Yoji had surfaced, and I had accidentally used her childhood nickname. For Kobato, at an age when she wanted badly to seem grown-up, perhaps that was a little humiliating.

lines.japanese: 「あ……うんじゃあ、せっかくだし……もらうね」
lines.english: “Oh... Well, then, since you went to the trouble... I'll take it.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　ああ、はい、どうぞ」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. Yes, please do.”

lines.japanese: 一転、頭を下げあう兄妹。なんだかよく分かんないけど、機嫌を損ねたわけじゃないみたいだからいいや。うぉんむ、うぉんむ。やはり姫には笑顔がお似合いだ。
lines.english: In an instant, brother and sister were bowing to each other. I did not quite understand, but she did not seem offended, so all was well. Hrrm, hrrm. A smile suited the princess best.

lines.japanese: はにかみながらソーセージを口に運ぶ小鳩はとても可愛かった。
lines.english: Kobato looked utterly adorable as she shyly lifted the sausage to her mouth.

lines.japanese: い、いや、この場合の可愛いっていうのはヘンな意味じゃねえからなブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。
lines.english: N-no, I didn't mean adorable like *that*. Anybody says I did, I'll fucking kill you, asshole.

lines.japanese: 「えへへ」
lines.english: “Hee hee.”

lines.japanese: はむはむとパンをかじる小鳩。
lines.english: Kobato nibbled at her bread.

lines.japanese: しばらく俺は、はむはむする小鳩を観察することにした。
lines.english: For a while, I decided to observe Kobato nibbling.

lines.japanese: ああ、しかし可愛いなあ、うちの小鳩は。見ているだけで穏やかな気分になってしまうぞ。
lines.english: Oh, but our Kobato truly was adorable. Merely watching her filled me with serenity.

lines.japanese: はむはむ。
lines.english: Nibble, nibble.

lines.japanese: はむはむ。
lines.english: Nibble, nibble.

lines.japanese: 「食べないの？」
lines.english: “Aren't you going to eat?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 箸を置いてはむってる小鳩を見ていたら、とても不思議そうな顔をされていた。
lines.english: I had put down my chopsticks to watch Kobato nibble, and now she was looking at me as if I were terribly strange.

lines.japanese: ああ、会話か。日本家庭の朝餉らしく、兄妹水入らずの会話がしたいんだな小鳩は。分かる、分かるぞ。そういうことならお兄ちゃんとてやぶさかではないぞ。
lines.english: Ah, conversation. Kobato wanted some good old-fashioned brother-and-sister time over breakfast. I understood. Perfectly. Her big brother was only too happy to oblige.

lines.japanese: 「あ、これ、いいパンでしょ。何もつけなくてもおいしいもんね」
lines.english: “This is good bread, isn't it? It tastes nice even without anything on it.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちの中で、過去「兄妹水入らずの会話」とやらに挑んだ経験があるのはタカシだけだ。ここはタカシの言葉を借りることにした。
lines.english: Of all of us, only Takashi had ever tried making breakfast conversation with his sister. I decided to borrow his words.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どうした小ば……」
lines.english: “Hm? What is it, Koba—”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は急に黙ったと思ったらすぐに立ちあがった。すたすたと白い靴下が畳を渡っていく。
lines.english: Kobato suddenly fell silent, then rose at once. Her white-socked feet marched briskly across the woven mats.

lines.japanese: あ、あれっ？　どうしたんだ小鳩……ま、まさかいまお兄ちゃんの言動に不快な点が！？　お、おいタカシ、どういうことだ。おまえの記憶通りやれば兄妹水入らずじゃないのか。
lines.english: H-huh? What's wrong, Kobato? C-could something your brother just said or did have upset you!? H-hey, Takashi, what's going on? Wasn't following your memories supposed to let us have some time alone as brother and sister?

lines.japanese: 一瞬青ざめたが、すぐにそれは杞憂だと知れた。
lines.english: I went pale for an instant, but soon discovered that my fears were groundless.

lines.japanese: 小鳩が小走りで戻ってくるや、マーガリンといちごジャムとメイプルシロップとツナマヨ風味のスプレッドを、ひとつずつコトリ、コトリ、コトリと俺の前に並べていった。
lines.english: Kobato hurried back with margarine, strawberry jam, maple syrup, and a tuna-mayonnaise spread, setting them before me one by one with four little clinks.

lines.japanese: ずらり。彼女の手が、目の前に並んだビンたちを示している。好きなものを塗れってことか。
lines.english: An entire row. Her hand indicated the containers arrayed before me. I was to spread on whatever I liked.

lines.japanese: 「うっ、うううっ……！」
lines.english: “Oh... Ohhh!”

lines.japanese: 俺は形而上の涙を噴射して歓喜にむせび泣いた。なんと、なんという優しくて気の利く子なんだろう。いますぐ結婚したい。
lines.english: I sprayed metaphysical tears and choked upon my joy. What a kind and thoughtful girl she was! I wanted to marry her this instant.

lines.japanese: ともあれ麗しき姫のご厚意はひとつたりとも無駄にできない。俺はマーガリンやらジャムやらの蓋を開けるや、パンとバターナイフを手に片っ端から塗りたくっていった。
lines.english: In any event, not one kindness offered by the radiant princess could go to waste. I opened the margarine, the jam, and all the rest, took up bread and butter knife, and slathered them on one after another.

lines.japanese: 「え、えええっ！」
lines.english: “Wh-what!?”

lines.japanese: 「そそっ、そんなぜんぶ塗らなくても……味が怪奇なものになっちゃまうよっ」
lines.english: “Y-you don't have to use *all* of them! It's going to taste like some kind of horror show!”

lines.japanese: なんか小鳩がうろたえてるけど、とにかく兄妹水入らずを再開しよう。ええと、たしかタカシはこのあと……。
lines.english: Kobato seemed upset for some reason, but for now I would resume our intimate sibling conversation. Let's see. After this, Takashi had said...

lines.japanese: 「さっきの続きなんだけどさ、これって結構いいパンだよね。あれかな、やっぱり、パン屋さんのパンってやつ。どこのお店？」
lines.english: “Back to what I was saying: this really is good bread, isn't it? Is it from a bakery? Which one?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、それは花水木通りに新しくできたパン屋さんのパンで、店長さんもとっても親切……ってそんなこといいから、そのパンをなんとかしないとだぁめー！」
lines.english: “Y-yes, it’s from the new bakery on Flowering Dogwood Street, and the manager is very kind—but forget that! You have to do something about that bread!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あの店。へえ、そうなんだ。いいね。うち、常連になろっか。店長さんもいいひとなら言うことないよね」
lines.english: “Oh, that place. Really? Nice. Maybe we should become regulars. If the manager's a good person, what more could you ask?”

lines.japanese: 「いいから、そういうのいいからパンをなんとかしないと、このままでは大変なことになりかねます」
lines.english: “Never mind that! You have to do something about the bread, or this could become a catastrophe!”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうか、こういうプレーンでも美味しいパンは素材の味を楽しんだ方がいいかもね。さすが小鳩はいいこと言うなあ。偉いからご褒美にこれあげるね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. With bread this good plain, maybe it's better to enjoy the natural flavor. Good point, Kobato. Since you're such a good girl, you can have this as a reward.”

lines.japanese: 俺は七色に染まった不気味パンを小鳩の皿へ渡し、自分のパンにはさらっとマーガリンだけ塗った。
lines.english: I transferred the sinister rainbow-colored bread to Kobato's plate, then spread my own with a modest layer of margarine.

lines.japanese: 「ううん、美味しいなあ。やっぱり迷ったときにはいつだって無難な選択が一番だよ……あれっ、どうした小鳩、早く食べないと遅刻しちゃうぞう」
lines.english: “Mmm, delicious. Whenever you're in doubt, the safest choice is best... Hm? What's wrong, Kobato? If you don't hurry and eat, you'll be late.”

lines.japanese: 「むぅー……いいよ、今日からお兄ちゃんの朝ごはんには、キュウリとトマトしか出さないから」
lines.english: “Hmph... Fine. Starting today, Big Brother’s breakfast will be nothing but cucumbers and tomatoes.”

lines.japanese: そりゃまた可愛い報復だなあ。ははは、ちょっと意地悪しすぎちゃったか。俺は兄妹水入らずの空気に微笑みながら、小鳩のパンを自分のそれと交換しようとした。
lines.english: What an adorable reprisal. Ha ha ha. Perhaps I had teased her a little too much. Smiling at the intimate mood between brother and sister, I reached to exchange Kobato's bread for mine.

lines.japanese: しかし一瞬早く彼女はパクついていた。
lines.english: But she took a bite an instant before I could.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、無理しなくていいんだぞう。そんな下品なジャンクフードは小鳩に合わない。伽楼羅にでも食わせておきゃ──」
lines.english: “Come now, you don't have to force yourself. Such vulgar junk food is beneath Kobato. Let Karura eat it or—”

lines.japanese: 「……あれ、意外とおいしい」
lines.english: “...Huh. It's surprisingly good.”

lines.japanese: まさかの好評だった。
lines.english: Against all expectation, it had earned a favorable review.

lines.japanese: 「マジで」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 気を使ってくれたのか……それとも単にゲテモノ食いなのかしら。
lines.english: Was she sparing my feelings...? Or did she simply have a taste for culinary abominations?

lines.japanese: 「毎日はつらいけど、一回だけなら試してみるといいかも」
lines.english: “It would be hard every day, but it might be worth trying once.”

lines.japanese: 「き、機会があれば」
lines.english: “I-if the opportunity arises.”

lines.japanese: どうやら本気みたいだ。自分で食わせといてなんだけど、すこし彼女の味覚が心配になった。
lines.english: She appeared to mean it. I had made her eat the thing myself, but I was beginning to worry about her palate.

lines.japanese: 叔父さん叔母さん、ごめんなさい。もし羽田家の小さなシェフがゲテモノ料理に目覚めてしまったら、それはたぶん俺のせいです。
lines.english: Uncle, Auntie, forgive me. If the Haneda family's little chef awakens to the art of cooking abominations, it will probably be my fault.

lines.japanese: 歩きなれたはずの通学路をスキップするような足取りで歩いた。
lines.english: I followed what should have been a familiar route to school with a skipping gait.

lines.japanese: 見慣れたはずの景色なのに、見慣れぬ景色という所感が混じってくる。へえ、あんなところに電柱あったのかあ。わあ、あの家はいつもモモヒキばかり干しているなあ。
lines.english: Though the scenery ought to have been familiar, the impression of seeing it for the first time kept intruding. Oh, so there was a utility pole there. Goodness, that house always had long underwear on the line.

lines.japanese: なんだか子供のころに戻ったみたいで、目に映るものすべてが新鮮かつ驚きの対象だ。
lines.english: It was as though I had become a child again. Everything that entered my eyes was fresh and astonishing.

lines.japanese: ああもう、なんだかむずむずしてきた。子供のころみたいに、この新鮮な驚き、世界に自分がいるという歓び、いま止めどなく溢れる感情、それらすべてを大きな声と体全体で表現したい。
lines.english: Oh, now I could feel it wriggling inside me. As when I was a child, I wanted to express it all with my whole body and the loudest voice I possessed: this fresh astonishment, the joy of existing in the world, every emotion now overflowing without end.

lines.japanese: うおおお、生きてるって素晴らしいィィィー！
lines.english: Ooooooh, what a glorious thing it is to be alive!

lines.japanese: ま、もちろん言わないけどね。ここは奈落じゃないんだ、自重しろよ、俺の中の約二名。
lines.english: Naturally, I did not say it aloud. This was not the Abyss. The approximately two of you inside me needed to show some restraint.

lines.japanese: はっ！　しまった、自重していたはずなのに、見知らぬ子供が奇異の目を向けている！？
lines.english: Ah! Damn. I thought I *had* shown restraint, yet an unfamiliar child was staring at me strangely.

lines.japanese: そうか、どうやら声は抑えていたつもりが、顔には出ていたらしい。
lines.english: Apparently, though I had kept my voice down, everything had shown on my face.

lines.japanese: ああ、いいなあ、子供は。そんな穢れのない瞳でまっすぐに見つめることができる。一切の打算も遠慮もない。ひとはいつから、ひとの目を見ることに躊躇を覚えるんだろう。
lines.english: Ah, children were wonderful. She could stare straight at me with such unclouded eyes, without calculation or reserve. When did people begin to hesitate before meeting another person's gaze?

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Yes, yes.”

lines.japanese: 俺はしみじみ頷きながら子供の前に屈みこんだ。
lines.english: Nodding with deep emotion, I crouched before the child.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんおなか痛いの？」
lines.english: “Mister, does your tummy hurt?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、お兄ちゃんは感動していたんだ。素晴らしいぞ、君の小さな目には、まだ余計なフィルターがかかっていない。いつか大人となってしまう前に、どうかひとつでも多くのものをその目に捉えておくれ」
lines.english: “No. I was moved. Your little eyes are magnificent: no needless filters have yet descended over them. Before you grow into an adult, I pray that you capture as much of the world as you can with those eyes.”

lines.japanese: 俺はこぶしを固めて力説した。
lines.english: I clenched my fist and delivered this impassioned speech.

lines.japanese: しかし幼い頭脳にはまだ早かったようだ。
lines.english: It appeared the subject was premature for her young mind.

lines.japanese: 「そうか、じゃあ分かりやすく行こう。さあ、お兄ちゃんと一緒にお手々を広げ、元気いっぱい声を出そうじゃないか。さん、はい──」
lines.english: “I see. Let us make it simpler. Come, spread your arms with me and shout with all your strength. Ready, and—”

lines.japanese: <8>\「──生きてるって素晴らしいィィィ！」
lines.english: “—what a glorious thing it is to be aliiiive!”

lines.japanese: 「あははは」
lines.english: “Ahahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「しおりっ」
lines.english: “Shiori!”

lines.japanese: Ｘ字状に四肢を伸ばしたところで、オサレな邸宅から血相変えた母親が走ってきた。まあ当然か。
lines.english: Just as I stretched all four limbs into an X, a horrified mother came running out of a stylish-looking house. Understandably enough.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな、お嬢ちゃん！　今日も一日張りきっていこう！」
lines.english: “Farewell, young lady! Let's give today everything we've got!”

lines.japanese: 目つぶしピースを向けると、母親は覆いかくすように子供の前へ立って俺の姿を遮った。お見送りごくろうさまです、お母さんも行ってらっしゃい元気よく。
lines.english: When I jabbed my eye-poke peace sign at the girl, her mother stepped in front of her and blocked me from view. Thank you for seeing me off. Have a lively day yourself, ma'am.

lines.japanese: 「ママ、あのひと面白い」
lines.english: “Mommy, that man is funny.”

lines.japanese: 「しっ！」
lines.english: “Shh!”

lines.japanese: 振り向きざま子供と目が合った。彼女は親に隠れながら、こっそり俺に目つぶしピースを返してきた。きっと幼稚園でも広めてくれるに違いない。俺は満足しながら悠々と朝の住宅街を突きすすんだ。
lines.english: When I glanced back, the child's eyes met mine. Half-hidden behind her mother, she secretly gave me the eye-poke peace sign right back. No doubt she would spread the gesture through her kindergarten. Satisfied, I strode majestically onward through the morning streets.

lines.japanese: こっちの世界はいいなあ。素晴らしいものがそこらじゅうに転がっているなあ。
lines.english: This world was wonderful. Marvelous things lay scattered everywhere.

lines.japanese: 駅に向かう緩やかな坂の下り道で、ふと足を止めた。いや、べつに靴紐がほどけたわけじゃないぞ。
lines.english: I abruptly stopped on the gentle downhill slope leading toward the station. No, my shoelace had not come undone.

lines.japanese: この先鋭的な住宅街の中にあって、前時代的な景観を残している商店。ガラス窓の小さな入口に人影が見えた。
lines.english: Amid this aggressively modern residential district stood a shop that preserved the look of another age. A figure occupied its narrow glass-fronted entrance.

lines.japanese: そういえばここは級友・山科京の家だったな。最近知ったばかりだが。
lines.english: Come to think of it, this was the home of my classmate Miyako Yamashina. I had only recently learned that.

lines.japanese: む。そうだ。卒業文集の作業で同じ班になったことだし、一言声をかけておくか。朝の挨拶を交わすことは、人間誰しも気持ちいいだろうからな。
lines.english: Hm. Of course. Since we were in the same group for the graduation anthology, perhaps I should say a word to her. Surely every human being found pleasure in exchanging morning greetings.

lines.speakerEn: Old Woman at the Tobacco Shop

lines.japanese: だけど店先にいたのは俺の知らない顔だった。
lines.english: But the person at the storefront was a face I did not know.

lines.japanese: まあ朝はみんな忙しいからな、山科京はもう家を出たのかもしれない。じゃなかったら、体が弱くて欠席がちな彼女のこと、今日も部屋で寝込んでいるか──
lines.english: Mornings were busy for everyone. Perhaps Miyako Yamashina had already left. Or, frail and frequently absent as she was, perhaps she was ill in bed again today—

lines.japanese: ──俺はフゥと前髪を吹きあげながら、そのままたばこ屋を通りすぎた。
lines.english: I blew my bangs upward and continued past the tobacco shop.

lines.japanese: 「明日も覗いてみるか……」
lines.english: “Maybe I'll peek in again tomorrow...”

lines.japanese: なんとなくそんな気持ちにさせる朝のたばこ屋だった。
lines.english: There was something about the tobacco shop that morning that left me feeling so inclined.

lines.japanese: 一時間目は担任・恩田教諭の授業だった──
lines.english: First period was taught by our homeroom teacher, Mr. Onda—

lines.japanese: ──と思う。ぶっちゃけあまり聞いてなかった。
lines.english: —I think. To be honest, I was not listening very closely.

lines.japanese: 新しい知識を学ぶことに興奮にも似た歓びはあったのだが、一方で教師の淡々とした講談を退屈だと訴える気持ちも強かった。多数決の結果、２対３で授業なんかつまらないということになった。
lines.english: Learning something new brought a pleasure close to exhilaration. At the same time, another part of me insisted the teacher's flat lecture was a bore. By a vote of three to two, the motion that class sucked was carried.

lines.japanese: かと言って授業を抜けだすわけにもいかず、俺はあいだを取って、机にノートを広げたまま別のことを始めた。自分の一日の予定を洗いなおしてみたのである。
lines.english: Yet I could hardly walk out, so I took a middle course: I left my notebook open on the desk and began doing something else. Specifically, I reviewed the structure of my day.

lines.japanese: 改めて円グラフにしてみると、今更ながら、これまでのスケジュールに相当の無理があったことを思いしらされた。
lines.english: Laying it all out as a pie chart, I was struck anew by just how unreasonable my schedule had been.

lines.japanese: 日中はタカシの学校。放課後に鷲介のバイト。深夜、始発の出る時間までは隼人の現場仕事──
lines.english: Takashi's school during the day. Shusuke's job after classes. Hayato's work sites late at night, until the first trains began to run—

lines.japanese: ──毎日必ずこの通りに≪交替≫があったわけではないし、体に限界が来て強制的に睡眠を取らされ、結果どこかの≪シフト≫が飛ぶことはわりとあった（だから鷲介や隼人は長期バイトが続かなかった）。
lines.english: The *switches* had not followed this exact pattern every day. Fairly often the body reached its limit and forced us to sleep, wiping one of the *shifts* from the schedule. That was why Shusuke and Hayato could never hold down a long-term job.

lines.japanese: とはいえ、これじゃいつでも眠くて当然だ。こんな生活を続けていてはガタが来る。あ、そうそうネットで見たんだけどね、睡眠不足は万病のもとらしいよ。
lines.english: Still, no wonder I had always been sleepy. A life like this would wear the body to pieces. Oh, yes—I read online that sleep deprivation is the root of every disease.

lines.japanese: まあ、これまで世話になったひとへの恩義もあるし、急にアルバイトをやめるわけにはいかないだろう。しかし、様子を見つつ出勤日を減らすとか、なんらかの策を講じないとまずいな。
lines.english: I owed debts to the people who had looked after me, and could not quit my jobs without warning. But I would have to take some measure—reduce my working days while watching how things went, perhaps.

lines.japanese: そんなことを考えているうちに終業のチャイムが鳴った。
lines.english: While I considered the matter, the bell rang to end class.

lines.japanese: うーん……そう簡単には結論でないか。じゃあ、この問題はひとまずペンディングとして──
lines.english: Hmm... Guess there's no easy answer. I'll leave this pending for now—

lines.japanese: ──あァ？　ペンディングってなに。あー保留ってことだけど。じゃ保留って言えよ、いちいち面倒くせえ横文字使うな、外人かてめえは。あーコラおまいらケンカすんなてー。
lines.english: The hell's ‘pending’? Oh, it means on hold. Then say *on hold*. Quit using annoying foreign words for everything. What are you, a foreigner? Hey, hey, you guys, no fighting.

lines.japanese: 「委員長。羽田君」
lines.english: “Class representative. Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「終わりです。号令を」
lines.english: “Class is over. Lead the closing.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田？　ああ、そっか俺か」
lines.english: “Haneda? Oh. Right, that's me.”

lines.japanese: 呆けて遅れていたら、教室のところどころから不満や苛立ちのうめきが聞こえた。
lines.english: As I sat there dazed and slow to respond, groans of complaint and irritation rose from several parts of the classroom.

lines.japanese: 「みんな、申しわけない！」
lines.english: “Everyone, my apologies!”

lines.japanese: 俺は深々と頭を下げてから号令をかけた。
lines.english: I bowed deeply, then called the class to order.

lines.japanese: ううむ、この思考散漫癖はなんとかせねば日常生活に支障をきたすな……。
lines.english: Hmm. Unless I did something about this tendency toward scattered thought, it would interfere with daily life...

lines.japanese: 「ねえ羽田風」
lines.english: “Hey, Haneda-style.”

lines.japanese: 休み時間、教室を出ようとした俺に危険人物ランクＢが声をかけてきた。昨日にしてもそうだが、俺──というかタカシは、渡来明日香からこんな軽々しく話しかけられるような間柄にあっただろうか。
lines.english: During the break, Threat Level B called out just as I was about to leave the classroom. Yesterday had been the same, but had I—or rather, Takashi—ever been close enough to Asuka Watarai for her to address me so casually?

lines.japanese: 俺は警戒心を強めて腕を組んだ。
lines.english: My guard rose, and I folded my arms.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ渡来」
lines.english: “What do you want, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「呼び捨てしないで」
lines.english: “You could at least call me Miss Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「なあに明日香ちゃん」
lines.english: “What is it, sweet little Asuka?”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり呼び捨てでいい。ちょっと話したいことがあるんだよね」
lines.english: “Actually, Watarai is fine. There's something I want to talk about.”

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香が俺に話だと？　ろくな予感がしないぞ。俺の中の５分の４がガンガン警鐘を鳴らす。恋するタカシには気の毒だが、こうなれば残り５分の１の意思はほとんど残らない。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai wanted to talk to me? Nothing good could come of it. Four-fifths of me rang alarm bells at full volume. I felt sorry for lovestruck Takashi, but under the circumstances that final fifth scarcely retained a will of its own.

lines.japanese: 結果、俺は渡来明日香を避けることにした。
lines.english: The result was that I chose to avoid Asuka Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「すまん、いまちょっと急いでるんだ」
lines.english: “Sorry, I'm in a bit of a hurry.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、急いでるってなに、どこ行くの」
lines.english: “Oh? In a hurry to do what? Where are you going?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはまだ考えてない」
lines.english: “I haven't thought of that yet.”

lines.japanese: 「おちょくってんのか」
lines.english: “Are you making fun of me?”

lines.japanese: 「というよりだな、渡来明日香と話すのは危険な気がするんだ。だっておまえ、なんか企んでるだろうブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “More accurately, speaking with Asuka Watarai strikes me as dangerous. You're plotting something, aren't you? I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「……あのさあ、羽田君になりきろうとかそういう気は微塵もないの？」
lines.english: “...Do you have even the slightest intention of trying to pass for Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、分からないやつだな。俺は羽田君以外のなに者でも……ん、そうか、なるほどな」
lines.english: “As I keep telling you, I am nothing other than Haneda... Hm. I see.”

lines.japanese: 「なにが」
lines.english: “See what?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君になりきる、か。よし、それいただきだ」
lines.english: “Pass for Haneda, you say. Good. I'll use that.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんね渡来さん。おれ、ちょっと急いでるんだ。だから君とは話せなくて」
lines.english: “Sorry, Watarai. I'm in a bit of a hurry, so I can't talk to you right now.”

lines.japanese: 俺がタカシ風の困り笑いをみせると、渡来明日香は一瞬驚いたあと悔しそうな表情をした。
lines.english: When I gave her a Takashi-style troubled smile, Asuka Watarai looked startled for an instant, then frustrated.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君みたいな顔しないでっ」
lines.english: “Don't make that Haneda face!”

lines.japanese: 「しろと言うからしたのに、理不尽なやつだな……」
lines.english: “You told me to, and now you object. What an unreasonable creature...”

lines.japanese: 握りこぶしを固める渡来明日香をあとに、俺は席を立って教室をあとにした。
lines.english: Leaving Asuka Watarai with her fist clenched, I rose from my seat and left the classroom.

lines.japanese: さて、渡来明日香から逃げてきたはいいが、目的がないのは本当だった。
lines.english: Now, escaping Asuka Watarai was all very well, but it was true that I had nowhere to go.

lines.japanese: 人生でも休み時間でも、とかく無から目的を定めるというのは難しいことなのだ。たしかタカシもそれで苦労していたはず。
lines.english: Whether in life or during a break between classes, choosing a purpose out of nothing is always difficult. Takashi himself had struggled with that, if I remembered correctly.

lines.japanese: 俺は携帯電話を開いて、タカシの課した自分目標を再確認した。信長の野心にチキンソテー定食……ううむ、我ながら小さいな。
lines.english: I opened my phone and looked over the goals Takashi had set himself. *Nobunaga’s Ambitions* and a chicken sauté set meal... Hmm. Even I had to admit those ambitions were small.

lines.japanese: その中の「６：クラスに友達を作る」という項目に目が止まった。
lines.english: My eye stopped upon item six: "Make friends in class."
“Friends!”

lines.japanese: なんだ、タカシもいいこと言うじゃないか。俺の中の５分の４は生来、友情というものに餓えていた。いますぐ友達百人作って、富士山のてっぺんでおにぎり食べたいなという夢や希望が湧きおこってきた。
lines.english: Well, now. Takashi could occasionally say something worthwhile. Four-fifths of me had been starved of friendship from birth. Dreams and hopes surged within me: I would make a hundred friends this instant, then eat rice balls with them on top of Mount Fuji.

lines.japanese: しかし悲しいかな、アレキサンダーやヤナポリ広場ならともかく、この学校において俺の友人はひとりしかいない。
lines.english: Sadly, however, while Alexander and Yanapoli Plaza were another matter, I had only one friend at this school.

lines.japanese: いや、ひとりっていうか……。
lines.english: Or rather, saying I had one friend might itself be questionable...

lines.japanese: いまの俺から客観的に見れば、果たして羽田タカシと森里和馬は友人関係と呼べる間柄だったか？　という疑問が残る。
lines.english: Seen objectively from my present perspective, could the relationship between Takashi Haneda and Kazuma Morisato truly have been called friendship?

lines.japanese: な、なに言ってるのさ、森里君は大事な友達だよ！　あァ？　あのうぜえ糞ロンゲだろ、トモダチなわけねーっつの。気持ち悪りぃことぬかすなコノヤロウ。ふむん、フェニックスの従士か。おぼろに知っておるぞ。
lines.english: Wh-what are you talking about? Morisato is a dear friend! Huh? That annoying long-haired piece of shit? No way he's a friend. Don't say creepy shit, asshole. Hrm. The Phoenix's retainer. I remember him but dimly.
“Ugh... Again...”

lines.japanese: ……また認識酔いだ。思考が分断されて頭がくらくらする。
lines.english: ...Perceptual motion sickness again. My thoughts split apart, and my head reeled.

lines.japanese: やはり統合は失敗だったのだろうか。いや、まだだ、そう簡単に認めるわけにはいかない。
lines.english: Had the integration been a failure after all? No. Not yet. I would not admit defeat so easily.

lines.japanese: 「考えてても仕方ない……友達かどうか確認しに行こう……」
lines.english: “Thinking about it won't settle anything... I'll go ask whether we're friends...”

lines.japanese: 俺はこめかみを押さえながら、よろよろ廊下を進んだ。目指すはフロアの一番端。特別強化学級３年Ｈ組。またの名をセントヘレナ。
lines.english: Pressing a hand to my temple, I staggered down the corridor. My destination was the far end of the floor: Special Advanced Class 3-H, otherwise known as Saint Helena.

lines.japanese: 「いや待て……でも、そうだ、あのロンゲはいま……」
lines.english: “No, wait... That's right. The long-haired bastard is...”

lines.japanese: Ｈ組のドアが見えたあたりで、ようやく酔いが醒めてきた。同時に隼人の記憶が甦る。
lines.english: By the time the door to Class H came into view, the sickness was finally beginning to clear. Hayato's memories returned with it.

lines.japanese: いま森里和馬がドアの向こうにいるはずはない。だってやつは香田亜衣をかばって撃たれたんだ。
lines.english: Kazuma Morisato could not possibly be beyond that door. He had been shot protecting Ai Koda.

lines.japanese: 傷は浅いって話だったが、それでもまだどこかの病院のベッドの上で、撃たれた足を吊って漫画雑誌でも読んでるはずだ。
lines.english: I had heard the wound was minor, but he should still be lying in some hospital bed, his injured leg suspended in the air while he read a comic book.

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫か、あいつ……」
lines.english: “I hope he's all right...”

lines.japanese: なんとはなしにＨ組のドアを開けてみた。名高き進学校に相応しくない風貌の学生たちがギャーギャー騒いでいる。いつ来てもガラの悪いクラスだ。
lines.english: For no particular reason, I opened the door to Class H. Students whose appearances were wholly unworthy of this prestigious preparatory school clamored inside. As ever, it was a rough-looking class.

lines.japanese: タカシの記憶が教える森里和馬の席には、菊の挿さった花瓶が置かれている。悪趣味だ。俺は失礼しますと言って教室の中へ入っていった。敵意に似た好奇の視線が集まる。
lines.english: Takashi's memory identified Kazuma Morisato's desk. A vase holding a chrysanthemum stood on it. Tasteless. I said, ‘Excuse me,’ and entered the room. Looks of curiosity tinged with hostility gathered upon me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれあれ～ッ？　キミ、羽田クンじゃない？　なにしてンのこんなトコで！」
lines.english: “Well, well! Aren't you Haneda? What're you doing in a place like this?”

lines.japanese: 菊の花瓶を拾いあげたところで、ガタイのいい男がずんずん近寄ってきた。誰だこの無軌道な若者は……ああ、一年のとき同じクラスだったような。
lines.english: I had just picked up the vase when a heavily built boy came striding toward me. Who was this lawless young man...? Ah. We might have shared a class in our first year.

lines.japanese: 「よう、久しぶり。森里君に会いに来たんだけど、今日は休みみたいだな」
lines.english: “Hey, long time no see. I came to see Morisato, but it looks like he's out today.”

lines.japanese: 俺が森里和馬の机を指すと、男は鏡餅みたいな頭を傾かせて俺を上から下まで睨めまわした。
lines.english: When I indicated Kazuma Morisato's desk, the boy tilted his head—a stack of New Year's rice cakes—and glared me up and down.

lines.japanese: 「ははは、おいおいどうした若人、そんなに熱い視線で俺を見て。まあ、いいからコレ園芸部に返しといてくれ。誰かが森里君の席に置きわすれちゃったみたいなんだ」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha. What is it, young man? Such a burning gaze. Anyway, return this to the gardening club, would you? Somebody seems to have left it on Morisato's desk.”

lines.japanese: 鏡餅の裏からもうひとり、瓢箪みたいな小男がやってきた。こっちもかすかに見覚えがある。
lines.english: Another boy emerged from behind the rice cakes, this one small and shaped like a gourd. He too seemed faintly familiar.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、君でもいいや。はいコレ、返しといて。水すくなくなってるから、ちゃんと入れてあげなきゃ駄目だぞ。お花さん可哀想じゃないか」
lines.english: “Ah, you will do just as well. Here, please return this. The water is running low, so be sure to fill it. The poor flower deserves better.”

lines.japanese: しかしふたりとも花瓶を受けとってくれない。笑ってるのか怒ってるのか微妙な顔で、ひたすら俺を見下ろしている。
lines.english: But neither boy accepted the vase. With expressions poised somewhere between laughter and anger, they continued to stare down at me.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、黙ってちゃ分かんないだろう。まあ、忙しいなら仕方ない、俺が返してくるか。えーと、園芸部って部室どこだっけ」
lines.english: “Hey, I can't tell what you want if you won't say anything. Well, if you're busy, I guess I'll return it myself. Uh, where's the gardening club's room again?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、つーか……とりあえずオモテ出て話しようじゃん。ここじゃなんだからさ」
lines.english: “No, I mean... Let's go outside and talk first. This isn't really the place.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　なんだなんだ、元クラスメイト同士、思い出話に花でも咲かせたいのか？　いいぞ、大歓迎だ。君も友達がいないんだろう、ははは、俺がなんでも聞いてやるぞう！　ああそこの君、じゃあこれお願いします」
lines.english: “Hm? What's this? Former classmates looking to let fond memories bloom? Splendid! You are most welcome. You have no friends either, do you? Ha ha ha! I shall listen to all your troubles. Ah, young lady over there—please take care of this.”

lines.japanese: 見物していたヤンキー化粧の女子に花と花瓶を任せ、のしのし歩きだしたふたりのあとを追った。
lines.english: I entrusted the flower and vase to a girl watching in delinquent-style makeup, then followed the two boys as they lumbered away.

lines.japanese: 「いや、ビビったわ。マジビビったわ。なに、羽田クンこんな時期にイメチェン？」
lines.english: “Man, you shocked me. Seriously. What's this, Haneda? Reinventing yourself this late in the year?”

lines.japanese: 「おっ、気付いてくれたか、嬉しいぞ。そうなんだ、二年間続けてきた物憂げな美少年キャラは飽きたから、薔薇色青春ＢＯＹに切りかえた。いつでも友達募集中、以降シクヨロぴょん」
lines.english: “Oh, you noticed! I'm delighted. I grew tired of the melancholy pretty-boy character I'd played for two years, so I switched to Rose-Colored Youth Boy. Friends wanted at all hours. Nice ta do biz with ya, bunnykins.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、なんだその目はー。友達にそんな目を向けるやつがあるか、ハハハこのやんちゃ坊主め、ずびしっ。ああ、そんなことより君らの親友森里君はどうしてる？」
lines.english: “Come now, what's that look? Friends don't look at each other that way. Ha ha ha, you little rascal. Bop! More importantly, how is your bosom friend Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 「いやつーか、和馬しばらくガッコ来てねーし」
lines.english: “I mean, Kazuma hasn't come to school for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう。なぜ」
lines.english: “Indeed? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「いやなんか？　入院してるって話は聞いたけど、詳しいことは知らねーし。あのロンゲ、診療内科とか行ってたらしーし、案外そっちで入院してんじゃねーの？」
lines.english: “I dunno. Heard he's in the hospital, but I don't know the details. That long-haired freak was seeing some psychosomatic doctor or whatever, right? Maybe that's what he's hospitalized for.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。すげーじゃん和馬。メンヘラ和馬じゃん」
lines.english: “Seriously? That's amazing. Kazuma's a total head case.”

lines.japanese: 「こらこら、親友にそんなこと言うやつがあるか、ええ？　言っていい冗談と悪い冗談があるだろう、謝りなさい」
lines.english: “Come now. You don't speak that way about a close friend. There are acceptable jokes and unacceptable ones. Apologize.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょい待てよ、なに、羽田クンさ、いつからそんな態度してんの？」
lines.english: “Hold up. Haneda, when'd you start acting like this?”

lines.japanese: 「つーか空気読んでよ。さっきタムラ君なんかキレかけて超睨んでたんですけど」
lines.english: “I mean, read the room. Tamura was glaring at you so hard back there, he was about to lose it.”

lines.japanese: 「うん？　誰だそれ。なんだ、その子も俺と友達になりたかったのか。なんだなんだ、言ってくれよおい、水臭いじゃないか」
lines.english: “Hm? Who is that? Did he want to become my friend too? Why didn't he simply say so? Come, now. No need to stand on ceremony.”

lines.japanese: 俺は親愛の情をこめてふたりの肩をばしばし叩いた。しかしあっけなく払われてしまった。
lines.english: I clapped the two of them heartily on the shoulders in an expression of affection. My hands were promptly brushed away.

lines.japanese: 「ぷはっ、何、なにコレ、俺ら羽田クンに超ナメられてねえ？」
lines.english: “Pfft! What the hell is this? Is Haneda seriously looking down on us?”

lines.japanese: 鏡餅の吹きだす声が聞こえた。にわかに空気が重くなる。参ったな、俺はこんなにも友好的な態度で臨んでいるのに。
lines.english: I heard the rice cake burst out laughing. The air abruptly grew heavy. How troublesome. I had approached them with such friendliness.

lines.japanese: 「ナメられてんね、これはもうカンペキ下に見られてんでしょ。ハァ、あの羽田クンがねえ～？」
lines.english: “He's looking down on us. Definitely thinks he's above us now. Man, *Haneda*, of all people?”

lines.japanese: 「なァ？　あのブルガリ買いに走ってたＤＴ羽田がだよ？　どうなのこの口の利き方。しかも俺ら眼中ねーみてえじゃん。なあ待ってよ羽田クン」
lines.english: “Right? This is Virgin Haneda, the errand boy who used to run out and buy Bulgari. What's with that mouth? Acting like we aren't even worth noticing. Hey, wait up, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: がしっと肩を掴まれた。タカシの嫌いな、敵意の握力だ。
lines.english: A hand clamped down upon my shoulder. The grip of hostility, which Takashi hated.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、待ってるぞ。どうした、なんかあんのか」
lines.english: “Yeah, I'm waiting. What's up? You need something?”

lines.japanese: 「なんかあんのじゃないでしょ。なに、おまえ？　一年のとき俺らのジュース買いに行ってた羽田クンだよね？」
lines.english: “Don't give me that. You're Haneda, the guy who used to buy our drinks in first year, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか！　あのとき立てかえといた金を返してくれるのか。いや、悪いなあ、なんか催促に来たみたいで。じゃあハイ、ちょうだい」
lines.english: “Oh, I get it! You're here to pay me back for covering you that time. Sorry, now it looks like I came to collect. All right, hand it over.”

lines.japanese: 「持ってねえよ、クソが」
lines.english: “I don't have it, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「分かった。じゃあ待ってるから財布取ってきてくれ。休み時間終わっちゃうからなるべく急いでね」
lines.english: “Got it. I'll wait here, so go get your wallet. Break's almost over, so try to hurry.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、森里くぅ～んなんつってヘコヘコしてた羽田クンが、なに俺らに命令してくれちゃってんのよ」
lines.english: “Oh, look at this. Haneda, who used to bow and scrape and whine, 'Morisatooo,' is giving *us* orders now.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい命令だなんて、人聞きの悪いこと言わないでくれよ。俺は同級生のあいだで威張ったり威張られたり、そういう勘違いがいちばん嫌いなんだ。森里君にしたって、彼は俺の友達だ、追随した覚えはないぞ」
lines.english: “Come now, ‘orders’ makes it sound so ugly. I hate this delusion that classmates should lord it over one another or submit to one another. As for Morisato, he is my friend. I don't recall ever being his lackey.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶはっ！　ぎゃはははは、なに、なに言ってんのコイツ、面白すぎんだけど！」
lines.english: “Pfft! Gyahahahaha! What is this guy even saying? This is too funny!”

lines.japanese: 「つーかアレじゃん？　美しー友情ってやつじゃん？　ホラ和馬もさあ、そもそもハブられだしたの、羽田んコトかばったからじゃん」
lines.english: “I mean, isn't this beautiful friendship? Kazuma only started getting frozen out because he stood up for Haneda, remember?”

lines.japanese: 「自分がパシらせてるうちは気付かなかったんだろうな。俺らが羽田イジり始めたら、急に手のひら返して『くだらねーことしてんなよ』だもんな。人間が中途半端なんだよ。そりゃウザがられるわ」
lines.english: “Didn't notice a thing while *he* was the one using Haneda as his errand boy. Soon as we started messing with Haneda, he flipped around and went, ‘Quit wasting your time.’ The guy's half-assed all the way down. No wonder everybody got sick of him.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだって！？」
lines.english: “Wh-what did you say!?”

lines.japanese: 俺の中の５分の１が衝撃を受けた。
lines.english: One-fifth of me reeled from the revelation.

lines.japanese: そして別の５分の１が後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。なんだ、あいつが学校からドロップアウトしたのはタカシのせいだったのか。
lines.english: Another fifth scratched roughly at the back of my head. So Takashi was the reason he had dropped out of school life.

lines.japanese: 「んで、アレだろ？　そのあと孤立しちゃって、ゾク入ったり精神病院通ったりだろ？」
lines.english: “And after that, he got all isolated, joined a gang, started seeing a shrink, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃははは、和馬チョーウケんだけど」
lines.english: “Gyahahaha! Kazuma's fucking hilarious.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、しょーもな。そーゆーことかよ。ったく、言えよあの糞ロンゲ。ちったあいいトコあんじゃねーか」
lines.english: “Hah. Lame. So that's how it was. Damn long-haired prick should've said something. Guess he had one or two decent qualities after all.”

lines.japanese: 「つかなに笑ってんだよ、いまは羽田がなんで調子コイてんだって話だろ」
lines.english: “Why are you smiling? We're talking about why Haneda suddenly thinks he's such hot shit.”

lines.japanese: 「そーだよ羽田クン、なに笑ってんのよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, Haneda. What're you smiling about?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、すまん。ちょっと俺の中の美談好きが、勝手に満足しちゃったみたいだ」
lines.english: “Ah, forgive me. The part of me that enjoys a touching story appears to have satisfied itself without permission.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、過去の過ちに固執しても先へは進めん。『汝の敵を愛し、迫害するもののために祈れ』。俺の座右の銘だ。だからおまえたちを赦そう。その代わりおまえたちも反省し、森里君にきっちりと謝罪するんだ」
lines.english: “Still, clinging to past wrongs prevents us from moving forward. ‘Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.’ Those are the words I live by. Thus, I forgive you. In exchange, reflect upon your conduct and apologize properly to Morisato.”

lines.japanese: 「つーかマジでワケわかんないんですけど、羽田どーしたらいきなりこんな調子コケんの？　ぶってんじゃん、チョー大物じゃん」
lines.english: “I seriously don't understand this. What happened to Haneda that he's suddenly acting so full of himself? Look at him putting on airs. What a big man.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。すげーじゃん羽田。プレジデント羽田じゃん」
lines.english: “Seriously. That's amazing. President Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、そうか？　いやあ、そんなに誉められると照れるな。でも俺なんてそんな大した人間じゃない、おまえらと同じちっぽけな人間だ。はははは」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! You think so? Goodness, all this praise is embarrassing. But I'm no one of importance. I'm merely another insignificant human being, just like you. Ha ha ha ha!”

lines.japanese: 三人の声が重なって、張りつめた空気に変化が生じた。
lines.english: Their voices overlapped, and the taut atmosphere changed.

lines.japanese: 「ザケてんじゃねーぞコラァ！」
lines.english: “Quit fucking around!”

lines.japanese: 鏡餅のこぶしがクレーンのように持ちあがり、ハンマーのように振りおろされた。
lines.english: The rice cake's fist rose like a crane arm and came down like a hammer.

lines.japanese: <8>\「ウヴァアァァァー！」
lines.english: “Uvaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: しかしそれが届くより早く、俺の右手が相手の腹へ喰いこんでいた。
lines.english: But before it could reach me, my right hand drove into his stomach.

lines.japanese: 「おぅエッ！」
lines.english: “Oghk!”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、自分でも何が起こったか分からなかった。大柄な体が派手に崩れる音を知覚したころ、ようやく自分の体が条件反射的に運動してしまったのだと気付いた。
lines.english: For an instant, I did not understand what had happened. Only when I registered the heavy body collapsing with a crash did I realize that my own had moved by conditioned reflex.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああッ！？　すすす、すまん、つい誰かをやっつけてやりたいと思う気持ちが漏れでてしまった！」
lines.english: “Ah—ahh!? I-I-I'm sorry! Somebody's desire to beat you down leaked out!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……ええっ！？」
lines.english: “Wh... what!?”

lines.japanese: 残された瓢箪男は、表情を泣きだしそうに歪ませたまま立ちすくんでいた。世界が平和でありますように。世界が平和でありますように。俺はおじいさんの呪文を唱えて、原始的な情動を必死に抑えこんだ。
lines.english: The remaining gourd stood frozen, his face crumpled on the verge of tears. *May peace prevail on Earth*. *May peace prevail on Earth*. I repeated the old man's incantation and desperately suppressed my primitive impulses.

lines.japanese: ふぬん……いかんぞ、これは。これではまるで統合が成功しておらぬようではないか。ばふんばふん。
lines.english: Hrm... This was no good. At this rate, one might almost think the integration had failed. Bafun, bafun.

lines.japanese: 「は、はははッ！　なあに仕方ない、男同士ときにはこうした手段で絆を深めることもあるものさ！」
lines.english: “Ha—ha ha ha! Well, it can't be helped. Sometimes men deepen their bonds by such means!”

lines.japanese: 俺はファイティングポーズをとって自分をごまかした。
lines.english: I raised my fists and tried to bluff my way through it.

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ次は君の番だ！　受けて立つぞ、存分にかかってこい！　シッ、シシッ！」
lines.english: “Now it is your turn! I shall face you. Come at me with all your strength! Hss! Hss-hss!”

lines.japanese: しかし俺が一歩踏みだすと、残された男は三歩下がってぶんぶん首を横に振った。
lines.english: But when I stepped forward once, the remaining boy retreated three steps and shook his head furiously.

lines.japanese: あれ？　ダチの仇ィ、とか言って飛びかかってくるかと思ったのに、意外と薄情なやつだな。まあ、校内で騒ぎを大きくされたら困るのはこっちだから助かるけど。
lines.english: Huh? I had expected him to leap at me shouting, ‘For my buddy!’ or something. Surprisingly heartless. Still, that helped me. I would be in far more trouble if he made a scene inside the school.

lines.japanese: 「うむ、賢明だぞ。腕力では何も解決しないからな」
lines.english: “Mm. A wise decision. Physical force settles nothing.”

lines.japanese: 俺はもっともらしいことを言って自分を棚にあげた。
lines.english: I spoke with great solemnity while setting my own conduct comfortably aside.

lines.japanese: 「ところで君、俺は森里君の見舞いに行きたいんだが連絡先を知っているか」
lines.english: “Incidentally, I wish to visit Morisato in the hospital. Do you know how to contact him?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……携帯電話の番号なら……」
lines.english: “Y-yeah... I have his cell number...”

lines.japanese: こうして俺は森里和馬のケー番を入手した。
lines.english: And so I obtained Kazuma Morisato's phone number.

lines.japanese: さあ、用も済んだしさっさと逃げよう。現場には学生の目がちらほらあるからな。校内暴力などといって教員に通報されてはまずい。
lines.english: My business was done. Time to flee. A few students had seen the incident. It would be disastrous if they reported me to the faculty for violence on school grounds.

lines.japanese: いったん背を向けたものの、しかしどうしても一言残したくて振りかえった。
lines.english: I had already turned away, but there was one thing I could not leave unsaid. I looked back.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに君たちより森里君の方が強かったぞ」
lines.english: “Incidentally, Morisato was stronger than either of you.”

lines.japanese: この目で見た俺が言うんだから間違いない。彼は柳木原フレイムバーズの幹部を相手に、殴られても殴られても立ちあがる、不屈の闘志を持っていたからな。
lines.english: I had seen it with my own eyes, so there could be no mistake. Against an officer of the Yanagihara Flame Birds, he had risen no matter how many times they struck him. His fighting spirit was indomitable.

lines.japanese: Ａ組の教室へ戻ると、すぐにいくつかの視線が俺に集中した。遠慮がちな囁き付き。
lines.english: The instant I returned to the Class A classroom, several gazes converged upon me, accompanied by hesitant whispers.

lines.japanese: ひょっとしていまの事件の噂が、もうこの教室まで届いているんだろうか。肩をすぼめるような姿勢で席へ着くと、畏怖や好奇の目の中からひとりが抜けでてきた。
lines.english: Could word of the incident already have reached this classroom? I took my seat with shoulders drawn in, and one person stepped out from among the looks of fear and curiosity.

lines.japanese: 「羽田ァー」
lines.english: “Hanedaaa.”

lines.japanese: げっ、高内昌子……！
lines.english: Gah! Shoko Takanouchi...!

lines.japanese: 「あんたさっきＨ組のやつらとなんか話してなかった」
lines.english: “Were you talking to some guys from Class H just now?”

lines.japanese: げっ、やっぱりその話！　くそっ、見られてたのか。しかし認めるわけにはいかない。バレていようがいまいが隠しとおしてやろう。
lines.english: Gah! It *was* about that! Damn it, had she seen me? But I could not admit anything. Whether she knew or not, I would hide it to the bitter end.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、ちょっとな。友達に会いに行ってたんだ」
lines.english: “Yeah, sort of. I went to see a friend.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 高内はいちど視線を逸らしたあと、またすぐに俺を見て意味ありげに笑った。
lines.english: Takanouchi looked aside once, then immediately turned back to me with a suggestive smile.

lines.japanese: 「なにがあったのか知らないけど、いいじゃん」
lines.english: “Dunno what happened, but I like it.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なにがだ？」
lines.english: “What? What is?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいよ羽田。あんたずっと今のままでいなって」
lines.english: “No, this is good, Haneda. Stay like this from now on.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、言われるまでもなく俺は羽田だが」
lines.english: “I'm Haneda whether you tell me to be or not.”

lines.japanese: 「だーから、そじゃなくて……ま、いいや。いっつもそういう風に偉ッそうにしてればいいんだよ」
lines.english: “That's not what I mean... Ah, never mind. Just keep acting all high and mighty like this.”

lines.japanese: 「副委員長はもうすこし偉ッそうさを抑えた方がいいと思うぞ」
lines.english: “I think the assistant representative should tone down the high-and-mighty act a little.”

lines.japanese: 「ええーッ、ひっど～い」
lines.english: “Whaaat? That's so meeean!”

lines.japanese: 「ひいいっ！」
lines.english: “Eek!”

lines.japanese: 高内昌子がまるで女子のような反応をするので、思わず声をあげてしまった。
lines.english: Shoko Takanouchi had reacted almost like an actual girl, and the shock forced a cry from me.

lines.japanese: 「あわ、あわわわわ……なんだそれは、新手の嫌がらせのつもりか。効果抜群じゃないか、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。貴様なにが狙いだ」
lines.english: “Wh-what is that...? Is this some new form of harassment? It is devastatingly effective. I'll fucking kill you, asshole. What are you plotting?”

lines.japanese: 「なに羽田、やっぱりセージュン系とか好きなん」
lines.english: “What, Haneda? You like the sweet and wholesome type after all?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、セージョウなひとが好きです」
lines.english: “No. I prefer normal people.”

lines.japanese: 「そっかそっか、へーなるほどねえ」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. I see. Very interesting.”

lines.japanese: ひとつも納得するようなことは言ってないはずなのに、高内昌子はうんうんと頷きながら席へ戻っていった。
lines.english: Though I was certain I had said nothing that should satisfy her curiosity, Shoko Takanouchi nodded repeatedly as she returned to her seat.

lines.japanese: さっぱり意味が分からない。分からないけれど、何故だか、言いようのない悪寒が俺の背筋をつたっていった。
lines.english: I understood nothing. And yet, for some reason, an indescribable chill ran down my spine.

lines.japanese: 「高内はああ言ってたけど、私は認めてないから」
lines.english: “Takanouchi may have said that, but *I* still don't accept you.”

lines.japanese: 放課後、みんながいなくなるなり彼女はやって来た。
lines.english: She came to me the instant everyone else had left after school.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、交渉したいんだけど、一度でいいから羽田君と話をさせてくれないかな」
lines.english: “Listen, I'd like to negotiate. Just once, could you let me talk to Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 女の口調は穏やかだったが、その語気には必死な含みが窺えた。ちょっと（当社比５分の１ぐらい）気の毒には思ったが、相手が敵か味方か不透明な以上、そうやすやすと懐柔されるわけにはいかない。
lines.english: Her tone was mild, but desperation showed through it. I did feel a little sorry for her—about one-fifth as sorry, by our internal metric—but while I could not tell whether she was friend or foe, I could hardly let myself be won over.

lines.japanese: 「おお、構わないぞ。俺が羽田君だ、さあ渡来、なんでも話してくれ」
lines.english: “Certainly. I am Haneda. Come, Watarai, speak to me of anything you wish.”

lines.japanese: 俺は例によってバックレた。
lines.english: As usual, I played dumb.

lines.japanese: 「いや、偽物じゃなくて」
lines.english: “I mean the real one.”

lines.japanese: 例によってかわせなかった。
lines.english: As usual, it did not work.

lines.japanese: 「昨日から偽物偽物とうるさいやつだな。俺が羽田だと言ってるじゃないか。ひとを疑う子はお兄ちゃん許さないぞ」
lines.english: “You've done nothing but call me an impostor since yesterday. I told you, I am Haneda. Your big brother will not forgive such a suspicious child.”

lines.japanese: 「……分かった。交渉って言ったのは撤回する。命令するから羽田君を出して」
lines.english: “...Fine. I take back the part about negotiating. This is an order: bring out Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「くどい。羽田は俺だ。ほら見ろ、オレ羽田ガハハあー小便してー」
lines.english: “Enough. I am Haneda. Look: me Haneda, haw haw haw, man, I gotta piss.”

lines.japanese: 「おい渡来、何が小便だ、馬鹿なこと言ってるんじゃない。そんなことより、さっさと卒業文集の制作会議を始めよう」
lines.english: “Watarai, what is this talk of taking a piss? Don't be absurd. More importantly, let us begin our meeting on the graduation anthology.”

lines.japanese: 「そうれ、学級委員権限、発動！　作業に無関係な話ばかりする班員は、非協力的とみなして担任に報告しますよ尾ひれはひれ付けて！」
lines.english: “Behold—the authority of the class representative, invoked! Any group member who talks of nothing but irrelevant matters shall be reported to our homeroom teacher as uncooperative, with plenty of lurid embellishment!”

lines.japanese: 「なにその横暴！　この暴君！　ネロ！　始皇帝！　織田信長！」
lines.english: “What kind of tyranny is that!? Tyrant! Nero! Qin Shi Huang! Oda Nobunaga!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、渡来さん。ネットで見たんだけどね、ネロに関しては暴虐な性格という側面からだけじゃなくて、その施政には肯定的な評価もされているから、一概に暴君とは言えないようになってきてるんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, Watarai. I read online that Nero is no longer assessed solely in terms of his tyrannical character. Some aspects of his rule have received favorable reevaluation, so apparently we can no longer call him a tyrant without qualification.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……ひょっとして偽物というよりも、羽田君としての意識もある……それかその逆、とか？」
lines.english: “Oh... Maybe you aren't exactly an impostor. You still possess Haneda's awareness too... Or perhaps it's the other way around?”

lines.japanese: くっ、ぐぬぬ……やるな、プリンセス。なかなか洞察力が鋭いようだ。やはり油断は出来ない。
lines.english: Ngh. Grrr... Well played, Princess. Her powers of observation were formidable. I could not lower my guard.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どしたの、もしかして正解に近い？　いま結構焦ってるよね」
lines.english: “Hm? What's wrong? Did I get close? You're pretty flustered now, aren't you?”

lines.japanese: ていうか、よく気付いたな。
lines.english: Seriously, how had she noticed?

lines.japanese: 「……渡来って、そんなに俺と親しかったっけ？」
lines.english: “...Watarai, were you and I ever that close?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ。なにいきなり？」
lines.english: “Huh? Where did that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、なんか、ずいぶん俺のこと詳しいみたいだから。三年間クラスは一緒でも、あんまり会話らしい会話ってしたことなかったような気がするんだけど……」
lines.english: “You seem to know an awful lot about me. We've been in the same class for three years, but I don't remember us ever having much of a real conversation...”

lines.japanese: 言葉に詰まった。なんでだ。相変わらず見えない女だが、ひとまず黙らせたということになるのか。
lines.english: She faltered. Why? The woman remained as unreadable as ever, but had I at least succeeded in silencing her?

lines.japanese: 「分かった。よし渡来、今日のところは痛み分けということにしておこう」
lines.english: “I understand. Very well, Watarai. We shall call today's engagement a draw.”

lines.japanese: 「慣れ合わないで」
lines.english: “Don't get chummy with me.”

lines.japanese: 睨まれた。なんだ、情報源と仲良くなるのは諜報員にとって望むところだろうに。無駄に気位の高い女だな。
lines.english: She glared at me. An intelligence agent ought to welcome friendly relations with her source. What a pointlessly proud woman.

lines.japanese: 「よぉーし、それじゃあ会議を進めるぞう！　えー、我が班の担当は寄せ書きの回収と、写真ページのレイアウトと……」
lines.english: “All right! Then let us proceed with the meeting! Our group is responsible for collecting the class messages, arranging the photo pages, and...”

lines.japanese: 「でも他のふたりがいないと話が進まないよね」
lines.english: “But we can't really get anywhere without the other two, can we?”

lines.japanese: そんなことはない！　やる気次第だ、諦めるな渡来！
lines.english: That is not true! All depends upon our will. Do not surrender, Watarai!

lines.japanese: と高らかに叫びたい気持ちはあったが、それ以上にさっさと帰りたいという気持ちも強かった。
lines.english: Part of me longed to cry those words to the heavens. Yet the desire to go home at once was stronger.

lines.japanese: 「それもそうだな！　いいところに気が付いたぞ、さすがだな渡来！」
lines.english: “You're right! Good catch, Watarai! Sharp as ever!”

lines.japanese: 俺は人員不足につき撤収、という彼女の意見を可決することにした。
lines.english: I voted to adopt her proposal that we withdraw due to insufficient personnel.

lines.japanese: ごくごく簡単な打ち合わせだけ済ませて一応の格好は付けたのち、本日の集会は解散とした。
lines.english: After a very brief discussion sufficient to preserve appearances, we adjourned today's assembly.

lines.japanese: さて、次のプログラムだ。トイレにでも行って着替えるとしよう。
lines.english: Now for the next item in the program. I would change clothes in the restroom or somewhere similar.

lines.japanese: 駅へ向かう途中でふと思いだした。
lines.english: On the way to the station, I suddenly remembered something.

lines.japanese: そういえばさっき森里和馬の電話番号を聞いたんだった。
lines.english: I had obtained Kazuma Morisato's phone number earlier.

lines.japanese: 彼はいま入院中だ。ひとりで退屈してるんだろうか。俺の中の誰か（まあひとりしかいないが）が熱望しているので、うっかり携帯電話を開いて登録したばかりの番号を眺めてしまった。
lines.english: He was in the hospital. Was he bored there alone? Someone inside me—though there was only one of me—wanted to call so badly that I found myself opening my phone and staring at the newly registered number.

lines.japanese: しばしの逡巡ののち、通話ボタンを押してみる。やつがタカシの身代わりになったという心温まるエピソードのせいで、いまや俺たちの中にも反対する者はいなかった。
lines.english: After a moment's hesitation, I pressed the call button. Thanks to that touching story of Morisato taking Takashi's place as their target, no one within us objected now.

lines.japanese: ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ……。
lines.english: Beep... beep... beep... beep...

lines.japanese: ん、待てよ？　でも森里和馬はいま病院にいるんだよな、だとしたらケータイは電源を切らなくちゃいけないはずだから――
lines.english: Hm, wait. Morisato was in the hospital. In that case, his phone was supposed to be switched off—

lines.japanese: ぷるるるるっ……ぷつっ
lines.english: Brrring... click.

lines.japanese: 「あい、もしもし？」
lines.english: “Yeah, hello?”

lines.japanese: もっ
lines.english: M—

lines.japanese: <8>\　森里君だ！
lines.english: Morisato!

lines.japanese: 俺の中の一部分にぱあっと春の陽光が射し、その暖かさはたちまち氷を溶かすように全体へ拡がった。
lines.english: Spring sunlight flooded one portion of me, then spread through the whole, melting its ice with that warmth.

lines.japanese: 歓喜と興奮のあまり言葉を失う俺。
lines.english: Joy and excitement robbed me of speech.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし？　おい、なんだコレ……電波繋がってねえの？」
lines.english: “Hello? Hey, what is this...? Bad connection?”

lines.japanese: 胸に沁みいるそのアンニュイな声。間違いない、僕の大好きな森里君だ！
lines.english: That languid voice sank deep into my heart. There could be no mistake. It was my darling Morisato!

lines.japanese: どっ、どうしよう、森里君と話したいことは沢山あるんだ。
lines.english: Wh-what should I do? There were so many things I wanted to discuss with him.

lines.japanese: 「お、おれっ、あの、分かるかな、分かるよね、おれだよおれ」
lines.english: “I-it's me. Um, you know who, right? You recognize me. It's me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　いや分からないけど……んだよ、オトコかよ」
lines.english: “Huh? No, I don't... What, you're a guy?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　てめ、なんで分かんないんだよ馬鹿かサル、その糞うぜえロンゲむしりとって、仔ヤギに喰わすぞこのハゲ野郎。ああもう、ひどいよ森里君、なんでおれが分かんないの！　おれだよ、おれヨージだよっ！」
lines.english: “Huh? Why the hell don't you recognize me, you stupid ape? I'll rip out that fucking annoying hair and feed it to a baby goat, you bald bastard. Oh, this is awful, Morisato! How can you not know me? It's me! Yoji!”

lines.japanese: ああどうしよう。もし森里君が病院で退屈しているのなら、今すぐブルガリを買っていってあげよう。蛎崎うにのＣＤも、足立アナの写真集も買っていってあげよう。そう思って、僕はポケットの中の小銭をあさった。
lines.english: Oh, what should I do? If Morisato was bored in the hospital, I would go buy him Bulgari at once. I would buy him a Uni Kakizaki CD and a photo book of Announcer Adachi too. Thinking this, I rummaged through my pockets for loose change.

lines.japanese: 「つーか誰」
lines.english: “Seriously, who is this?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ちゃりんちゃりん。ショックのあまり小銭が散らばった。そうか、きっと久しぶりだから、僕の声を忘れてしまったんだ。そう、それだ。
lines.english: Coins scattered with a jingle. The shock had made me drop them. Of course. It had been so long that he had forgotten my voice. That had to be it.

lines.japanese: 「おっ、思いだして！　おれだよ、ヨージだよ！　ほら森里君がよくシャイニングウィザードの練習をしてくれた、クラスメイトのヨージだよ！」
lines.english: “R-remember! It's me, Yoji! Your classmate Yoji—the one you used to practice your Shining Wizard on all the time!”

lines.japanese: 「いや知らないけど……ちょっ、あんた落ちつけって」
lines.english: “I don't know any Yoji... Look, calm down.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもどうしよう、病院の中で電話なんかしてたら森里君が怒られちゃうよね」
lines.english: “Oh, but wait. If you're talking on the phone inside the hospital, won't you get in trouble?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いま屋上いっから」
lines.english: “Nah, I'm on the roof.”

lines.japanese: 「素晴らしい！　マーベラス！　病床の際にあってもマナーを最優先するそのジェントルマン精神！　さすが、レトルトカレーを撥ねちらさず開封できる男は心意気が違う！」
lines.english: “Splendid! Marvelous! Even from a hospital bed, you put manners above all else! What gentlemanly spirit! A man who can open a pouch of ready-made curry without spraying it everywhere is made of nobler stuff!”

lines.japanese: 「でもネットで見たんだけどね、最近は病院内での携帯電話使用禁止を疑問視する声もあがってるんだ。だって他にも電波を出す機械は沢山あるのに、ケータイだけ駄目なんておかしいじゃねえかブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Though I read online that people have recently begun questioning blanket bans on mobile phones in hospitals. Plenty of other machines emit radio waves, so why the hell should phones alone be forbidden? I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: しばらくの間があって、やがて電話の向こうからため息をつく音が聞こえた。
lines.english: After a long silence, I heard a sigh from the other end of the call.

lines.japanese: 「つかイタ電かよ」
lines.english: “So this is a prank call.”

lines.japanese: プツッ！
lines.english: Click!

lines.japanese: ああ、切られてしまった。残念だな、思いだしてもらえなかったか。
lines.english: Ah, he had hung up. What a shame. I had failed to make him remember.

lines.japanese: ていうか、ヨージじゃなくてタカシって言わないと分かるわけないじゃん。そう、それだ。
lines.english: Then again, of course he wouldn't understand unless I said *Takashi* instead of *Yoji*. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 俺は次に電話したとき何から話すべきか考えながら、うきうきと駅へ向かった。
lines.english: Thinking happily about what I should say first when next I called him, I made my way toward the station.

lines.japanese: ははは、友情って素晴らしいなあ！
lines.english: Ha ha ha! Friendship truly is a wonderful thing!
